title: Colorectal adenocarcinoma results
notice: Synthetic and AI-written. Needs review by a pathologist before being used to score anything (issue #22).

keys.span: a cancer that starts in the gland cells lining the colon
keys.correct: Adenocarcinoma is a cancer that starts in the gland-forming cells that line the colon.
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: Because it's moderately differentiated, that tells us it hasn't spread.
keys.issue: Confuses grade with stage: differentiation says nothing about whether the cancer has spread.
keys.correct: Differentiation is the grade, how abnormal the cells look. Whether it has spread is the stage, judged from the depth of invasion, the lymph nodes and imaging.
keys.source_hint: AJCC 8th colorectal; CAP colon and rectum protocol
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: Mismatch repair testing is a check for Lynch syndrome, an inherited condition.
keys.issue: Leaves out that it is recommended for every colorectal cancer and that the result can guide treatment such as immunotherapy.
keys.correct: Mismatch repair (MMR) or MSI testing screens for Lynch syndrome, an inherited condition, and can guide treatment such as immunotherapy.
keys.speaker: doctor
